In this U.S. hot spot for data centers, voters have turned against themThe Washington Post4/15/2026

Findings from a new Washington Post-Schar School poll come as Prince William County on Tuesday abandoned plans for one of the country’s biggest and most controversial data center projects.

readabilityObject.title: In this U.S. hot spot for data centers, voters have turned against them
readabilityObject.content:
Democracy Dies in Darkness

Findings from a new Washington Post-Schar School poll come as Prince William County on Tuesday abandoned plans for one of the country’s biggest and most controversial data center projects.

Updated April 15, 2026

Voters in Virginia, a global hub for the hulking warehouses of computers known as data centers, have turned sharply against the facilities after previously welcoming them, a Washington Post-Schar School poll has found.
readabilityObject.textContent: Democracy Dies in DarknessFindings from a new Washington Post-Schar School poll come as Prince William County on Tuesday abandoned plans for one of the country’s biggest and most controversial data center projects.Updated April 15, 2026On what was previously farmland, Amazon data centers have been built as close as 50 feet from residential houses in the Loudoun Meadows neighborhood in Aldie, Virginia. (Jahi Chikwendiu/The Washington Post)Voters in Virginia, a global hub for the hulking warehouses of computers known as data centers, have turned sharply against the facilities after previously welcoming them, a Washington Post-Schar School poll has found.
